text: Many government surveys assign PSU IDs locally within stratum. NHANES, example, assigns IDs 1 2 within every stratum — PSU 1 stratum 31 completely different unit PSU 1 stratum 32. account , surveycore treats PSU 1 stratum 31 PSU 1 stratum 32 cluster, produces incorrect variance estimates. Set nest = TRUE PSU IDs globally unique across strata (Lumley 2010, 28). quick diagnostic: number unique PSU values much smaller number strata, IDs almost certainly nested need nest = TRUE.

text: get_ratios() estimates ratio two weighted totals: R̂=∑iwiyi∑iwixi\hat{R} = \frac{\sum_i w_i \, y_i}{\sum_i w_i \, x_i} Variance estimated via delta method (linearization), equivalent survey::svyratio() (Lumley 2010). Ratios useful want estimate invariant scale weights — example, wages per hour, spending per household member, disease prevalence ratios.
code: # Ratio of systolic to diastolic blood pressure get_ratios(svy, numerator = bpxsy1, denominator = bpxdi1) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   ratio ci_low ci_high     n #>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <int> #> 1  1.74   1.71    1.76  6302 # Systolic/diastolic ratio by sex get_ratios(svy, bpxsy1, bpxdi1, group = riagendr) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   riagendr ratio ci_low ci_high     n #>      <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <int> #> 1        1  1.72   1.69    1.75  3115 #> 2        2  1.75   1.73    1.78  3187

title: Getting Started with surveycore
text: get_corr() estimates survey-weighted Pearson correlations two continuous variables. Confidence intervals use Fisher Z transformation, guaranteeing bounds (−1, 1). Pass three variables pairwise correlation matrix long format: row unique variable pair. r weighted correlation, p_value two-tailed t-test, df = n - 2 degrees freedom. Switch wide format familiar correlation-matrix layout:
code: # Correlation between systolic BP and diastolic BP get_corr(svy, c(bpxsy1, bpxdi1)) #> # A tibble: 1 × 9 #>   var1   var2       r ci_low ci_high   p_value statistic    df     n #>   <chr>  <chr>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <int> <int> #> 1 bpxsy1 bpxdi1 0.441  0.415   0.467 1.46e-298      39.0  6300  6302 get_corr(svy, c(bpxsy1, bpxdi1, bpxpls)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>   var1   var2         r  ci_low   ci_high   p_value statistic    df     n #>   <chr>  <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> <int> <int> #> 1 bpxsy1 bpxdi1  0.441   0.415   0.467    1.46e-298     39.0   6300  6302 #> 2 bpxsy1 bpxpls -0.122  -0.156  -0.0868   3.46e- 22     -9.72  6300  6302 #> 3 bpxdi1 bpxpls -0.0277 -0.0555  0.000135 2.77e-  2     -2.20  6300  6302 get_corr(svy, c(bpxsy1, bpxdi1, bpxpls), format = "wide") #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   variable bpxsy1  bpxdi1  bpxpls #>   <chr>     <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 bpxsy1   NA      0.441  -0.122  #> 2 bpxdi1    0.441 NA      -0.0277 #> 3 bpxpls   -0.122 -0.0277 NA

title: Getting Started with surveycore
text: common pattern survey analysis computing estimate subpopulation — adults aged 60 , particular racial group, one treatment arm study. physically subset data frame building design object. Removing rows changes cluster stratum structure produces incorrect standard errors (Lumley 2010, ch. 4). Use filter() instead. marks rows outside domain keeping design object cluster structure remains intact:
code: library(surveytidy)  # Mean systolic BP for adults aged 60 and older # The full cluster/strata structure is preserved for correct SEs svy |>   filter(ridageyr >= 60) |>   get_means(bpxsy1)

title: Create a Taylor Series Linearization Survey Design — as_survey
text: Creates survey design object using Taylor series (linearization) variance estimation. Supports simple random samples, stratified designs, single- multi-stage cluster designs, designs finite population correction. Uses tidy-select interface design variable arguments.

title: Create a Taylor Series Linearization Survey Design — as_survey
text: data data.frame containing survey responses. Must least one row unique column names. ids <tidy-select> Cluster (PSU) ID column(s). single-stage: ids = psu. multi-stage: ids = c(psu, ssu). Omit entirely simple random sampling. probs <tidy-select> Sampling probability column (single column, values (0, 1]). Converted weights = 1/probs stored internally. used together weights unless values consistent (weights == 1/probs). weights <tidy-select> Sampling weight column (single column, values strictly > 0). strata <tidy-select> Stratification variable column (single column). fpc <tidy-select> Finite population correction column (single column). Accepts either total population size (integer) sampling fraction (numeric, 0–1). contain NA. nest Logical. TRUE, PSU IDs treated nested within strata — .e., ID value two different strata refers two distinct PSUs. Set nest = TRUE PSU IDs globally unique (e.g., NHANES, PSU IDs restart 1 stratum). Requires strata specified. Default FALSE.

title: surveycore 0.1.0
text: as_survey() creates survey_taylor objects tidy-select interface (ids, weights, strata, fpc, probs); supports Taylor linearization stratified, clustered, SRS designs. as_survey_rep() creates survey_replicate objects; supports BRR, Fay BRR, JK1, JK2, JKn, bootstrap, ACS, successive-difference replicate schemes. as_survey_twophase() creates survey_twophase objects; supports “full”, “approx”, “simple” two-phase variance estimation methods. update_design() modifies design variables existing survey object without reconstructing scratch; respects validate = TRUE/FALSE. get_means() returns weighted mean standard error via Taylor linearization replicate weights; respects getOption("survey.lonely.psu") single-PSU strata. get_totals() returns weighted total standard error using dispatch get_means(). Metadata setters: set_var_label(), set_variable_labels(), set_val_labels(), set_value_labels(), set_question_preface(), set_question_prefaces(), set_var_note(), set_variable_notes(). Single-variable setters automatically import haven "label" / "labels" attributes data frame column.
